title: Hackett proposes him for Masonry and dies
summary: Hinton recalls the Roosevelt Grill; Leeman says Hackett proposed him for the Masons, with Paul Whiteman signing, and mourns Hackett's death.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: That's a good idea, Cliff, and I know those records; I have some of them myself. And that one is a special one; I remember playing at the Roosevelt Grill down there, I was in one of the bands, also, so it was my good fortune to listen to you guys every night and to hear such good music that Dick Gibson was putting together in the Roosevelt Grill in those days -- and it is a good idea to make the suggestion that, for posterity, some of these records should be kept around, and reissued -- especially for the great playing of you and the magnificent Bobby Hackett and the very great Vic Dickson.

I'm going to add that Bobby Hackett proposed me for Masonary which was another beautiful thing in my life, and Paul Whiteman signed the papers, and I was a brother of Bobby Hackett's in more ways than one. When Bobby Hackett died a few years later on, I participated in a few jazz sessions across the country with Bobby, and when he died, the music business lost a great, great trumpet player, and I lost a most dear friend.
